title: Formatting and Consistent Style
learningObjectives: Describe how formatting helps readers scan and compare code.
Use line breaks to reveal logical structure.
Identify formatting inconsistencies that obscure code.
Separate formatting changes from behavior changes during review.

understand.concept: Formatting is the visual organization of source code: indentation, spacing, line breaks, braces, and alignment. Consistent formatting makes control flow and relationships easier to scan. A formatter or style guide can reduce debates and prevent mixed conventions. Formatting should clarify structure, not create artificial alignment that becomes fragile. When reviewing changes, separating formatting-only edits from logic changes helps reviewers focus and makes diffs easier to trust.
understand.whyItMatters: Readable, consistent code is easier to review, debug, and safely modify. These habits reduce unnecessary mental effort without replacing testing or design.
understand.analogy: Think of source code as instructions shared with a future teammate: clear labels and organization help them follow the route.
understand.analogyLimit: Analogies simplify collaboration; code still has precise rules, scope, and runtime behavior.

explain.narrative: Indent nested blocks consistently, leave meaningful space between sections, and avoid excessively long lines when a split improves comprehension. Use one established style throughout a file or project. Automated formatters are useful because they apply predictable rules, but the rules should be agreed upon and should not be mistaken for correctness checks.

commonMistakes: Using short or vague names that hide intent.
Applying personal style inconsistently with the project.
Treating formatting or comments as proof of correctness.
Making broad cosmetic changes mixed with logic edits.
Leaving comments or documentation stale after behavior changes.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Take a compact code sample with uneven indentation and missing spaces. Reformat it using one consistent rule set. Preserve all statements and operators. Compare the formatted version's diff. Verify the output or trace before and after is identical.

Reformat it using one consistent rule set.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Choose a 15–25 line script you wrote or invent one. Apply consistent indentation, whitespace, and line breaks. Avoid changing logic or identifiers. Record the formatting rules you followed. Explain why the new layout is easier to scan.

Change logic at the same time without explanation

questions.explanation: Smaller, focused diffs are easier to review.
